core_obligations: Modify X to a projective-immersion space.
Split the piece on the modification via the schemes theorem.
Push the splitting down through the closed-image and henselian arguments.
Verify the descended piece is proper with the right special fibre.
difficulty_reason: For (A, I) a henselian pair, X separated of finite type over A with special fibre X_0, and Y ⊂ X_0 open and closed proper over A/I, there exists W ⊂ X open and closed, proper over A, with W_0 = Y. The retained proof is complete: take a surjective proper modification phi : X' -> X with X' admitting an immersion into P^n_A via the weak Chow lemma (Cohomology of Spaces, lemma weak-chow); the schemes-side twin (More on Morphisms, lemma split-off-proper-part-henselian) supplies W' ⊂ X' with W'_0 = Y' = phi^{-1}(Y); the images Q_1 = phi(|W'|) and Q_2 = phi(|X' \ W'|) are closed by universally-closed permanence, Q_1 carries only proper closed-subspace structures (image-proper-is-proper); the intersection Q_1 x Q_2 maps closed into Spec A and henselianity forces any of its points to lie over V(I), contradicting W'_0 = Y' — so Q_1 is open and closed, and W = the corresponding subspace of X satisfies W proper with W_0 = Y by descent along the surjection. Retained author proof at lines 8493-8520.
